title: Attention Is All You Need: Transformer Architectures in Machine Learning
abstract: We propose the Transformer, a novel neural network architecture based entirely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on machine translation tasks demonstrate superior performance and training speed.
authors: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan N. Gomez, Łukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin
concepts: Artificial Intelligence, Transformers, NLP, Deep Learning

title: Deep Residual Learning for Large-Scale Image Recognition
abstract: Deeper neural networks are more difficult to train. We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those previously used. We evaluate residual nets with a depth of up to 152 layers on ImageNet.
authors: Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, Jian Sun
concepts: Deep Learning, Computer Vision, Artificial Intelligence

title: Genome Engineering via Early CRISPR-Cas Systems
abstract: Functional bacterial CRISPR-Cas systems can be engineered for targeted genome editing in human and mouse cells. We demonstrate Cas9-mediated gene knockout and precise homology-directed repair in eukaryotic genomes.
authors: Sophia Thorne, Michael Chang, Feng Zhang, George M. Church

title: Cas13 Trans-Cleavage Activity for Diagnostic Nucleic Acid Detection
abstract: CRISPR-Cas13 enzymes exhibit target-activated non-specific RNA cleavage. We harness this trans-cleavage activity to create SHERLOCK, a point-of-care diagnostic platform capable of attomolar viral RNA detection.
authors: Sophia Thorne, Robert Sterling, James J. Collins

title: Perovskite Solar Cells: Efficiency Limits and Stability Architectures
abstract: Organometal halide perovskites have rapidly emerged as leading candidates for next-generation photovoltaics. We evaluate carrier diffusion lengths, optical absorption boundaries, and moisture degradation prevention architectures.
authors: Li Wei, Carlos Gomez, Henry J. Snaith

title: Solid-State Sodium-Ion Batteries with High Voltage Polymer Electrolytes
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries offer an abundant alternative to lithium chemistry. We design a cross-linked polyether solid electrolyte maintaining high ionic conductivity at room temperature across 1000 charge-discharge cycles.
authors: Amara Chen, Jean-Pierre Dubois, Claire Meyer
concepts: Energy Storage, Solid-State Batteries, Renewable Energy, Sodium-Ion

title: 3D U-Net and ResNet Architectures for Volumetric Brain MRI Segmentation
abstract: Accurate volumetric segmentation of subcortical brain structures in multi-sequence MRI datasets is vital for tracking Alzheimer's progression. We present a 3D dual-pathway ResNet-U-Net deep network architecture.
authors: Elena Rostova, Sarah Lin, Olaf Ronneberger
concepts: Computer Vision, Medical Imaging, Deep Learning, Neurology

title: Satellite-Based Quantum Communications and Free-Space QKD
abstract: We report satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution (QKD) over distances up to 1200 kilometers using optical transceivers mounted on a low-Earth-orbit satellite, establishing quantum-secured wireless links.
authors: Marcus Vance, Hiroshi Tanaka, Jian-Wei Pan

title: Tandem Perovskite-Silicon Photovoltaics Exceeding 29% Efficiency
abstract: Integrating wide-bandgap perovskite top cells with textured silicon bottom cells overcomes single-junction Shockley-Queisser limits. We achieve 29.15% power conversion efficiency in a two-terminal tandem architecture.
authors: Li Wei, Hannah Schmidt, Steve Albrecht
concepts: Solar Cells, Clean Tech, Energy, Photovoltaics

title: Solid-State Sodium Electrolyte Conductivities at Room Temperature
abstract: NASICON-structured inorganic solid electrolytes exhibit high room-temperature ionic conductivity. We optimize grain boundary impedance to enable high-current density sodium-metal anodes.

title: Early Foundations of Convolutional Neural Networks for Medical Image Classification
abstract: Multi-layer convolutional feature maps provide translation-invariant representations for anatomical structures in digital radiography and MRI. We evaluate early CNN topologies on chest X-ray and brain scan benchmarks.
authors: Elena Rostova, David K. Miller, Yann LeCun
concepts: Deep Learning, Medical Imaging, Computer Vision

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Algorithms for Next-Generation Wireless Standard
abstract: As quantum computing capabilities advance, public-key infrastructure faces vulnerability. We evaluate lattice-based and code-based post-quantum cryptographic primitives suitable for low-latency 6G air interfaces.

title: Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution Principles in Fiber Networks
abstract: We analyze homodyne detection of coherent state optical signals for continuous-variable quantum key distribution across installed telecom optical fibers, proving secret key rates over 80 km.

title: Polymer Solid Electrolyte Interfaces for Rechargeable Batteries
abstract: Solid polymer electrolytes offer safety advantages over flammable liquid organic solvents. We synthesize poly(ethylene oxide) derivative networks incorporating lithium and sodium salts.
concepts: Energy Storage, Solid-State Batteries, Materials Science

title: Deep Learning Architectures for Early Detection of Alzheimer's Disease in MRI Scans
abstract: Early diagnosis of neurodegeneration in structural MRI relies on detecting subtle hippocampal atrophy. We introduce BioResNet-3D trained on ADNI cohort datasets achieving 94.2% sensitivity.
authors: Elena Rostova, David K. Miller, Sarah Lin
concepts: Deep Learning, Medical Imaging, Computer Vision, Neurology, MRI

title: Generative Multi-Agent Systems for Automated Cross-Disciplinary Scientific Discovery
abstract: We introduce BioAgent, an autonomous framework of specialized LLM agents trained on PubMed literature. BioAgent automatically synthesizes cross-disciplinary research and formulates verifiable hypotheses.
authors: Alexander Wright, Priya Sharma, Lucas Vance
concepts: Artificial Intelligence, LLM, Autonomous Agents, AI for Science
